currentContext.expansion: The Company's principal stated expansion is an upgrade and expansion of its lyophilisation capacity by 50%, undertaken to cater to rising global demand, with the project expected to be completed in calendar year 2026; management states this enhancement will support entry into regulated markets such as Europe and the UK. Alongside the capacity work, the Company is laying the groundwork for a branded business in the veterinary and human critical-care segments, and has ventured into Gynaecology and Assisted Reproductive Technology through a new division, FertiNova, focused on advanced IVF solutions and women's health therapies, which is said to have performed well in its initial launch. Geographic expansion is pursued by entering new international markets through collaborations with reputed partners, introducing new products in existing markets and building a robust marketing and distribution network within India; the animal-healthcare footprint dates from the 2023 acquisition of the animal healthcare business of Agilis Healthcare Private Limited, with FY2025-26 the third full year of operations. On the regulatory front, 24 new product registration applications were submitted during the year, 2 registrations were received and 5 renewed, with registration of 19 products expected in the upcoming financial year. Structurally, the NCLT Ahmedabad Bench sanctioned the Scheme of Amalgamation merging Lyka Export Limited into Lyka Labs Limited by order dated 16th March 2026.

risks.note: Named by management in MD&A 'Risks and Concerns' as one of the risks common to the industry. The business depends on product registrations and approvals — 24 new registration applications were submitted during the year with 19 registrations expected next year, and the Pregabalin Gel launch required CDSCO approval — so approval timing directly gates new-product revenue.

Named by management in MD&A 'Risks and Concerns'. The Board's report confirms it bit during the year: certain markets experienced foreign exchange fluctuations (alongside political uncertainty) because of which purchases were delayed.
Explicitly listed by management in MD&A 'Risks and Concerns' among the risks common to the industry.

risks.risk: Export demand concentrated in international Government tenders
risks.note: The Board's report states the export business did not meet expectations because international Government tenders had exhausted their budgets — a structural dependence on government tender cycles and their budget availability, outside the Company's control.

risks.risk: Geopolitical and political uncertainty in export markets
risks.note: The Board's report attributes delayed purchases in certain markets to political uncertainty; the MD&A macro commentary additionally flags continued geopolitical tensions, higher energy prices, trade protectionism and debt vulnerabilities in emerging economies.

risks.risk: Exposure to the subsidiary Lyka BDR International Limited
risks.note: The operating loss for the year is stated to arise primarily from a one-time impairment charge related to the Company's investment in, and outstanding loans given to, its subsidiary Lyka BDR International Limited, presented as an exceptional item — evidencing that the Company carries material credit and investment exposure to that entity.

The Company states it is engaged in only one segment, viz. pharmaceuticals, so there is no diversification outside the pharmaceutical cycle; growth depends on the human and veterinary healthcare businesses and on the new FertiNova (ART/IVF) division rather than on unrelated earnings streams.

Management explains the year-on-year movement in its key ratios by pointing to increased borrowings — the current ratio fell because of the increase in borrowings for the year, and the debt-equity ratio rose because of new loans availed during the financial year — while interest cover turned negative on negative EBIT.

risks.risk: Execution risk on the announced lyophilisation expansion and regulated-market entry
risks.note: The Company's growth plan rests on a 50% lyophilisation capacity expansion targeted for completion in calendar year 2026 to enable entry into regulated markets such as Europe and the UK; the benefit is contingent on that project completing to schedule and on the regulatory acceptance that follows.
